wasi.result: Both actual WASI jobs pass. Runtime and WASI tests are unchanged by the later native unload fixture repairs.

scope: All owned-value and kernel tests passed on six native hosts. The two overall Windows jobs failed only the new library-unload fixture export check. That fixture was repaired without changing runtime sources; its dedicated follow-up passed all six native jobs. This records allocation and cleanup probes, not full production acceptance, elapsed time, C/Rust parity, cache behavior, or dynamic register pressure. All managed-allocation failure points are exercised until success; native-buffer accounting does not inject system malloc failures. Semantic checks compare raw/optimized interpretation and native O1/O2, with tracing stress/reuse verification and checked ARC. Allocation probes disable tracing collection.

build.CCompiler: CC selects Clang; Windows uses pinned LLVM-MinGW 20261006. Exact paths and runner images are in job logs. No compiler-version-independent speed claim.
build.hardware: Native ARM64/AMD64 GitHub-hosted Linux/macOS/Windows runners named in each report. All native pointers are eight bytes; no CPU microarchitecture timing measurement.

kernelComparison.baseline: Only the kernel executor is replaced with immutable 21a621c699d11a84c05f955935dc95dcfb8adbf2:runtime/fwp_rt_kernel.c; the compiled probe and other runtime code are current. This is not a comparison of complete compiler revisions.
kernelComparison.workload: 8193 F64 values equal to their indices, multiplied by 0.5; elementwise output and ordered sum, with one/four requested workers. Inputs already exist when counting starts.
kernelComparison.removed: One native 65544-byte elementwise output and its full copy. The managed 65552-byte result array remains; worker arithmetic scratch and input-pointer table remain.
kernelComparison.reduction: Block sums and arithmetic order remain. One scalar per 4096-element block is allocated, plus per-worker workspace.
kernelComparison.peak: Native peak excludes managed objects, allocator metadata/test ledger headers, stacks, thread/runtime storage and resident memory. Concurrent scheduling changes peak worker overlap. Separate peaks must not be added as if simultaneous.
